rationale: Start with a broad gradient to observe all 10 compounds and locate their elution window. A moderate temperature and gradient duration provide a baseline for identifying critical pairs before narrowing the window.

Change only gradient duration to determine whether the two critical early pairs respond to a shallower slope. This diagnostic run will distinguish slope-sensitive overlap from selectivity limitations before optimizing temperature and run time.

Test the high-temperature endpoint at the original slope to measure temperature-driven selectivity changes in the crowded early cluster. Higher temperature should also shorten retention, leaving more room for a shallower gradient if needed.

Combine the favorable high-temperature selectivity with a shallower gradient to test whether the remaining R = 1.09 pair reaches baseline resolution. The last peak should remain close to 10 minutes, potentially giving full resolution without a substantial time penalty.

The remaining critical pair worsened with a shallower gradient, so test a steeper gradient instead. This will shorten the run and may improve that pair, while checking whether the neighboring R = 2.05 pair retains adequate resolution.

Test a higher starting organic fraction to change selectivity within the early cluster, since slope changes alone have not resolved its last pair. Keeping a 12-minute gradient provides more separation margin for the neighboring pair than the 8-minute method.

Increase the starting organic fraction one more step to extend the improvement in the remaining critical pair. The neighboring pair has resolution margin, and the last peak should remain comfortably below 10 minutes.

The maximum CRF is achieved; now shorten the gradient by one grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method. Keep the solvent window and temperature unchanged to isolate the effect on the two closest pairs.

Shorten the gradient another step to locate the speed limit for full resolution at this solvent window. Injection 8 remains the faster confirmed maximum-score method if either critical pair falls below 1.5.

Narrow the gradient window to give a slope between the fully resolved 10-minute method and the marginally unresolved 8-minute method. The last peak previously eluted near 0.64 organic, so a 0.85 endpoint should retain ample elution strength while potentially restoring full resolution.

Test whether another increase in starting organic fraction shortens retention while preserving full resolution. This probes the solvent-window limit, with injection 10 retained as the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Test a one-step temperature decrease against the fastest fully resolved method to measure local selectivity sensitivity. This will show whether a nearby temperature offers more resolution margin for further shortening.

Return to 60 C and test a shorter, narrower gradient whose slope is only slightly steeper than injection 10. The 0.70 endpoint lies above the estimated last-peak elution fraction, making this a targeted test for a faster maximum-score method.

Injection 13's rounded CRF masks a pair just below 1.5, so reduce the endpoint one step to restore resolution. The last peak should elute near the gradient end without a long hold, testing a compact fully resolved method.

With maximum-score methods secured, test the low-temperature endpoint for an alternative elution order that might permit faster full separation. The steep, high-organic gradient limits the risk of excessive retention while probing this unexplored selectivity regime.

Return to favorable high-temperature selectivity and lengthen injection 11's gradient one step to address its sole unresolved pair. This tests whether the higher starting organic fraction can support another fully resolved method with improved margin in the other critical pair.

Reduce the gradient slope slightly to push injection 16's R = 1.47 pair above 1.5 while retaining ample final solvent strength. This targets another maximum-score method, although injection 10 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved option.

With the fastest fully resolved region bracketed, test a more conservative maximum-score method with greater resolution margin. Extrapolation from the 10- and 12-minute gradients suggests the last peak should remain below 10 minutes while both critical pairs improve.

Test whether a shallower gradient at the higher starting organic fraction gives balanced resolution margins while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. Injection 10 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method; this run targets a more conservative maximum-score alternative.

Test whether injection 19's resolution margins permit a lower-temperature maximum-score method. Changing only temperature will assess selectivity sensitivity at this higher starting organic fraction, with enough retention-time margin to accommodate modestly later elution.

Injection 20 still flags a marginally unresolved pair despite its rounded score; slightly reduce the slope to seek genuine full resolution at 55 C. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, avoiding a time penalty.

Refine around injection 10, the fastest confirmed fully resolved method, by lowering the endpoint one step. This should add resolution margin to its R = 1.51 pair with only a modest retention-time increase, providing a fast maximum-score alternative.

Test the remaining endpoint between injection 10's fully resolved method and injection 9's slightly unresolved method. This directly checks whether retention can be shortened below 6.04 minutes while keeping every pair at R ≥ 1.5.

Back off the slope from injection 23 by increasing gradient duration one step, targeting full resolution with more margin than injection 10. This untested method should keep the last peak well below 10 minutes; injection 10 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score option.

Use the final injection to test a slightly shallower neighbor of injection 24, targeting additional resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. Injection 10 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved maximum-score method.
